title: The Ten Hymns of Synesius
author: Synesius of Cyrene (Stevenson trans)
description: The Ten Hymns of Synesius, Bishop of Cyrene, A.D. 410, in English verse by Alan Stevenson, LL.B., F.R.S.E., the Scottish lighthouse engineer to the Board of Northern Lighthouses and uncle of Robert Louis Stevenson (privately printed, 1865), with some occasional pieces. Synesius of Cyrene (c. 373-414), a student of the Neoplatonist philosopher Hypatia in Alexandria, became a Christian bishop while retaining his Platonic convictions. His hymns, written in Doric Greek lyric metres, fuse Neoplatonic metaphysics with Christian devotion: the One as Monad beyond all, the Trinity as Father, Son and Spirit understood through Platonic triads, the descent of the soul into matter and its ascent back to the divine, and prayers for liberation from the body's bonds. Stevenson's verse translation, with notes, is a rare Victorian rendering of these key texts of Christian Platonism.
